violations.explanation: The previous-page IconButton has no tooltip or semanticLabel, so screen readers announce it only as an unlabeled button.
The next-page IconButton has no tooltip or semanticLabel, so screen readers cannot convey its purpose.

violations.affected_code: onPressed: () async { if (_currentPage >= 1) { ... } }, icon: _currentPage == 0 ? const Icon(Icons.arrow_back, color: Colors.white38) : ...
violations.explanation: At the first/last page the buttons are only visually dimmed but onPressed remains non-null, so assistive technologies report them as enabled even though activating them does nothing. onPressed should be null to expose the disabled state.

The page indicator updates when pages change, but it is not wrapped in a live region (Semantics(liveRegion: true)), so screen reader users are not informed of the new current page after pressing navigation buttons.

violations.affected_code: const Icon(Icons.arrow_back, color: Colors.white38) / Text(... color: Colors.white)
violations.explanation: Hardcoded white and semi-transparent white colors ignore the theme; depending on the background they may fail contrast requirements. The background is not defined in this component.
